walkthroughs.body_html:
Theme 2: The UK Economy - Performance and Policies — a core area of A-Level Economics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Theme 2: The UK Economy - Performance and Policies brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Theme 2: The UK Economy - Performance and Policies.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The Laffer curve was popularised in:
Solow's growth model shows long-run growth driven by:
options: Capital accumulation
Technological progress
Population growth
Government spending
Structural unemployment is unemployment caused by a recession.
A negative externality is a tax on a business.
Unemployment caused by a mismatch between workers' skills/location and available jobs — often due to long-term economic change like deindustrialisation.
Structural unemployment is when people are too lazy to work.

mcqs.q: What are the functions of money?
options: Structural unemployment is when people are too lazy to work.
Money is only valuable if backed by gold.
Money is valuable because it is made of valuable materials.
Medium of exchange, store of value, unit of account, and standard of deferred payment — money must perform these to function as money.
A cost imposed on a third party not involved in the transaction — e.g. pollution from a factory affects neighbours who didn't choose to bear it.
A negative externality is something bad that happens to a business.
Structural unemployment is when people are too lazy to work.
A negative externality is a tax on a business.
